exampleAnswers.title: The Period of a Transformed Function

question.text: Calculate the period of the function $y = -\sec\left(\dfrac x 3-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right).$
question.explanation:
Given a function of the form $y = A\sec(Bx +C) + D,$ the period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{B}.$

In our case, we have that $B=\dfrac 1 3.$ Therefore, the period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{\left(\dfrac 1 3\right)}=6\pi.$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Range of a Transformed Function

question.explanation:
The range of $\csc x$ consists of two intervals: \[ \csc x \in (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty) \]

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore, \[ \csc\left(4x-\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) \in (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty). \]

We can split this into two inequalities: \[ \csc\left(4x-\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) \leq -1, \qquad \csc\left(4x-\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) \geq 1 \]

To find the range of $f(x),$ we consider both intervals separately.

  • Multiplying the first interval by $-1$ and adding $4,$ we get \begin{align*} &\csc\left(4x-\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right)\leq -1\\[5pt] &-\csc\left(4x-\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) \geq 1\\[5pt] &-\csc\left(4x-\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) +4\geq 1+4\\[5pt] &f(x)\geq 5. \end{align*}

  • Multiplying the second interval by $-1$ and adding $4,$ we get \begin{align*} &\csc\left(4x-\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) \geq 1\\[5pt] &-\csc\left(4x-\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right)\leq -1\\[5pt] &-\csc\left(4x-\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right)+4\leq -1+4\\[5pt] &f(x) \leq 3. \end{align*}

Combining both inequalities, we get \[ f(x) \geq 5, \qquad f(x) \leq 3. \]

Therefore, we conclude that the range is $f(x) \in (-\infty,3] \cup [5, \infty).$

example.title: Finding the Range of a Transformed Function

question.explanation:
The range of $\csc x$ consists of two intervals: \[ \csc x \in (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty) \]

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore, \[ \csc\left(4x + 5\right) \in (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty). \]

We can split this into two inequalities: \[ \csc\left(4x+5\right) \leq -1, \qquad \csc\left(4x+5\right) \geq 1 \]

To find the range of $f(x),$ we consider both intervals separately.

  • Multiplying the first interval by $2,$ we get \begin{align*} &\csc\left(4x+5\right) \leq -1\\[5pt] &2\csc\left(4x+5\right) \leq -2\\[5pt] &f(x)\leq -2. \end{align*}

  • Multiplying the second interval by $2,$ we get \begin{align*} &\csc\left(4x+5\right) \geq 1\\[5pt] &2\csc\left(4x+5\right) \geq 2\\[5pt] &f(x) \geq 2. \end{align*}

Combining both inequalities, we get \[ f(x) \leq -2, \qquad f(x) \geq 2. \]

Therefore, we conclude that the range is $f(x) \in (-\infty, -2] \cup [2, \infty).$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding Local Extrema of a Transformed Function

question.text: What is the value of $f(x) = -2\csc \left(x -\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right)+4$ at its local minimum points?
question.explanation:
On a negative branch of the graph of $y=\csc x,$ we have

\[ \csc x \leq -1. \]

The points where $\csc x = -1$ are local maximums of the graph of $y=\csc x.$ For now, we're interested in the local maximums (not local minimums) of $y=\csc x$ because we see that $f(x)$ contains a vertical reflection.

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore, \[ \csc \left(x -\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) \leq -1. \]

Multiplying the above inequality by $-2$ and adding $4,$ we get

\begin{align*} &\csc \left(x -\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) \leq -1\\[5pt] &-2\csc \left(x -\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) \geq 2\\[5pt] &-2\csc \left(x -\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) +4\geq 2+4\\[5pt] &-2\csc \left(x -\dfrac{\pi}{3} \right) +4\geq 6\\[5pt] &f(x)\geq 6. \end{align*}

Therefore, $f(x)=6$ at its local minimum points.

example.title: Finding Local Extrema of a Transformed Function

question.text: What is the value of $f(x) = -3\sec \left(3x \right)-5$ at its local minimum points?
question.explanation:
On a negative branch of the graph of $y=\sec x,$ we have

\[ \sec x \leq -1. \]

The points where $\sec x = -1$ are local maximums of the graph of $y=\sec x.$ For now, we're interested in the local maximums (not local minimums) of $y=\sec x$ because we see that $f(x)$ contains a vertical reflection.

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore, \[ \sec \left(3x \right) \leq -1. \]

Multiplying the above inequality by $-3$ and subtracting $5,$ we get

\begin{align*} &\sec \left(3x \right) \leq -1\\[5pt] &-3\sec \left(3x \right) \geq 3\\[5pt] &-3\sec \left(3x \right)-5\geq 3-5\\[5pt] &-3\sec \left(3x \right)-5\geq -2\\[5pt] &f(x)\geq -2. \end{align*}

Therefore, $f(x)=-2$ at its local minimum points.

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Domain and Asymptotes of a Transformed Function

question.text: What is the domain of the function $f(x) =-3\csc\left( \dfrac {x}{6} -\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
The domain of $y=\csc x$ consists of all values where $\sin x\neq 0,$ and is given by the expression

\[ x \neq n\pi, \] where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $-3\csc\left( \dfrac {x}{6} -\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left( \dfrac {x}{6} -\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right).$ This gives

\[ \dfrac {x}{6} -\dfrac{\pi}{3} \neq n\pi . \]

Solving for $x,$ we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac {x}{6} -\dfrac{\pi}{3}&\neq n\pi \\[5pt] \dfrac {x}6 &\neq \dfrac{\pi}{3}+ n\pi \\[5pt] x &\neq \dfrac{6\pi}{3}+6n\pi \\[5pt] x &\neq 2\pi+6n\pi. \\[5pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x \neq 2\pi+6n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.

example.title: Finding the Domain and Asymptotes of a Transformed Function

question.text: What is the domain of the function $f(x) = \sec\left(\dfrac{x}{2}+60^\circ\right),$ where $x$ is measured in degrees? Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
The domain of $y=\sec x$ consists of all values where $\cos x\neq 0,$ and is given by the expression \[ x \neq 90^\circ + n\cdot 180^\circ , \] where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $\sec\left(\dfrac{x}{2} +60^\circ\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left( \dfrac{x}{2} + 60^\circ\right).$ This gives \[ \dfrac{x}{2} +60^\circ \neq 90^\circ + n\cdot 180^\circ . \]

Solving for $x,$ we get \begin{align*} \dfrac{x}{2} +60^\circ &\neq 90^\circ + n\cdot 180^\circ \\[5pt] \dfrac{x}{2} &\neq 90^\circ + n\cdot 180^\circ -60^\circ \\[5pt] \dfrac{x}{2} &\neq 30^\circ + n\cdot 180^\circ \\[5pt] x &\neq 60^\circ+n\cdot 360^\circ. \end{align*}

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x \neq 60^\circ+n\cdot 360^\circ,$ where $n$ is an integer.

example.title: Finding the Domain and Asymptotes of a Transformed Function

question.text: What is the domain of the function $f(x) =-\csc\left( \dfrac {2x} 3 -\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
The domain of $y=\csc x$ consists of all values where $\sin x\neq 0,$ and is given by the expression

\[ x \neq n\pi, \] where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $-\csc\left( \dfrac {2x} 3 -\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left(\dfrac {2x} 3 -\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right).$ This gives

\[ \dfrac {2x} 3 -\dfrac{\pi}{6} \neq n\pi . \]

Solving for $x,$ we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac {2x} 3 -\dfrac{\pi}{6}&\neq n\pi \\[5pt] \dfrac {2x}3 &\neq \dfrac{\pi}{6}+ n\pi \\[5pt] 2x &\neq \dfrac{3\pi}{6}+3n\pi \\[5pt] 2x &\neq \dfrac{\pi}{2}+3n\pi \\[5pt] x &\neq \dfrac{\pi}{4}+\dfrac{3n\pi}{2}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x \neq \dfrac{\pi}{4}+3n\dfrac{\pi}{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.
